verdicts.claim: 1a. runs.csv has 115 scored runs on the 23 listed questions; 112 scored cells, 109 with one run, 3 with two, none with three
verdicts.reason: Independent recount (verify/v01_counts_log.txt [1], [4]): 233 rows, 115 scored runs, all with an estimate, on exactly the 23 listed questions; 112 (question, config) cells, 109 x 1 and 3 x 2 (jp_movers, kr_online, lhr_pax on v2.11g, none catastrophic).

verdicts.claim: 1b. 14 catastrophic scored runs on 8 questions, all thinking off; versions and commits as in PREREG B3 (3 of them on v2.11f)
verdicts.reason: Stored flag equals recomputed |ln err| > ln 2 on the same 14 runs; 8 questions; all thinking off, deepseek-flash; versions v2.1* x3, v2.1b, v2.1c-pre, v2.8r, v2.11f x3, v2.11g, v2.12a x2, v2.16e; each has n_same_config_scored = 1 (v01 [2]).

verdicts.claim: 1c. Pool B re-runs each catastrophic run's own configuration (same code, thinking, noown, question, mode)
verdicts.reason: runs.json matches every original on version, code commit, thinking, noown, question text and as_of; all originals were backtests; tags unique and absent from results/agent (v01 [7], [8]). Commit identity confirmed by content: each of the 10 commits has the same triangulate/ code (comment lines only) as the 24 other commits with the same author date and subject (v06). Corrections now in PREREG B3: the tree commit is the latest by committer date; the v2.8r tree 48e6b45 also adds the test2 questions (148 inserted lines in forecast.py), so worktrees.json's 'adds only BUGS.md' is incomplete; the 5 v2.1*/v2.1b originals were launched by probes/run_v2_backtests.py as 8 threads of one process sharing the fetch rate limiter, while the repeats are single CLI processes (v05 [c]); sensitivity without these 5 cells added (E3/R2); a run-time request-identity check on the first plan call's prompt_tokens added (E0).

verdicts.claim: 2a. HEAD's triangulate/ equals tag v2.17a (behaviourally); the runner freezes the tree hash
verdicts.reason: Not byte-equal: git diff v2.17a HEAD -- triangulate changes 2 comment lines (forecast.py, showcase_engine.py; commit 6c7f702), exactly as PREREG B1 states; HEAD:triangulate 7eaec1e4 vs tag tree f3cad700; no uncommitted change; is_peak only sets the price (v03).

verdicts.claim: 2b. Old-version invocation (python -m triangulate agent --question --tag --auto-approve [--ablate-own-history]) and result copying are right
verdicts.reason: CLI flags, RES path, ablation_tag, TRIANGULATE_KEY_FILE, cache key and file format identical at all tree commits (03 log, re-checked for fetch.py); results/forecast/summary.json and the LightGBM model files are tracked at those commits; no optional imports in triangulate code; copy_back copies only into a non-existing destination and raw pages without overwrite. Caveat: the v2.1*/v2.1b launcher difference of 1c.

verdicts.claim: 3. Runner: off-peak waiting, <= 3 runs, never two runs of one question, skip-existing, $30 stop, logging, no overwrite
verdicts.reason: Verified by reading and by dry runs (verify/dryrun_*_v_prereg.txt). Fixed in run_repeats.py: (1) api_rejected_400/404/422 only for a run without an estimate (otherwise a valid outcome would be re-run); (2) new infra class 'interrupted' (start, no end, no state.json, older than 2 x timeout), because a killed runner left runs neither re-runnable nor classified; (3) round N+1 refuses to start while round-N infra failures lack their once-only re-run; (4) leak_decide no longer drops questions with a prompt-token difference from the shift test; (5) end events log HTTP codes and the plan prompt_tokens. Offline tests on synthetic logs and answers all pass (verify/v04_runner_tests_log.txt); classify_infra on the 233 archive dirs still flags exactly the 7 *_402 runs.

verdicts.claim: 4a. Every analysis in section E is fully specified (metric, unit, test, interval, MDE, confirmatory status)
verdicts.reason: Gaps fixed in PREREG: ln 0 for identical estimates (floor s^2 = 1e-6 plus sensitivity); a row both 'different' and 'nearly equal' (now 'nearly equal (p < 0.05)'); reversed-sign results ('different, against the thesis'); R2 listed with pre-set labels but had none (now mean d_c = same-config B3 rescue minus a5 p_rescue_med3_any, sign-flip p, label); F2, M1, B1, S1 were 'secondary confirmatory' with no test (now descriptive); E3 denominator, no-estimate handling and 'both intervals' rule; E4 ties and the definition of 'drift detected'; E1 cell inclusion, why p0 = 10.2% (vs runs.csv 14/115 = 12.2%) and the clustering caveat; the G that applies to V1 (<= 21) and K1/K2 (17).
verdicts.correct_numbers: V1 G <= 21 (as-is questions with >= 2 core estimates); K1/K2 G = 17 (MDE about 0.72 SD)

verdicts.claim: 4b. The leakage-check decision rule is stated before data and implemented as stated
verdicts.reason: Stated (D3) and implemented as written, but the 'same request tokens' filter would have removed every question from the shift test exactly when the hosted model or tokenizer changed (the most leak-prone case), since the request text is identical by construction (05 log). Filter removed; the decision record flags n_prompt_tokens_differ and tokenizer_or_hosted_request_changed (tested). D5 now says how a repeated check is made and that transport/key/balance failures abort the check instead of producing invalid answers.

verdicts.claim: 4c. O2 is a single frozen statement with a lookup protocol
verdicts.reason: One primary (gate false alarms at 2x vs the archived naive answer) with a frozen scorer. Fixed: 'supports C2' on a single false alarm is weak (one-sided Fisher vs in-sample 0/82 needs about 2 false alarms on about 17 runs), so a strength rule was added; the past-only reading 'consistent with C2 if the interval overlaps 12.7%' could not fail and was dropped; lookup rules added for a third lookup (majority of three), approximate or bound statements, other time bases or aggregations (no_comparable_value) and earnings-call sources (googl_tokens). o2_score.py unchanged; it prints only the direction.

verdicts.claim: 4d. The literature coding scheme has rules for ambiguous cases
verdicts.reason: G4 covered most cases; added: S and T stated for some statistics only = P; 'each configuration run once' = S = Y with count 1; strata (a) same-configuration statistics vs (b) cross-version-only papers, because G2 (ii) admits ablation-only papers that would otherwise dominate the gap count. The population (77 + 9 = 86) is consistent with lit/verified_papers.json and TOPIC_DECISION section 6.

verdicts.claim: 5. The plan answers the claims it serves and reports the outcome that would hurt the thesis
verdicts.reason: Outcome 2 (as-is about equal to same-config, said in the abstract) was already defined. Added: P2 positive on pool A is also what the v2.17a ceiling produces, so it is read as an estimand difference only with the pool-B rows; which reading each pool-B direction cuts against; inconclusive and reversed primaries count towards neither or towards outcome 2; the 3-lane concurrency is stated as a departure from TOPIC_DECISION O3 'one at a time'. Unresolved: no same-config aggregation measurement with headroom that is not conditioned on a catastrophic original.

verdicts.claim: 6. Budget arithmetic (expected about $18, high about $29, hard stop $30; about 22 run-hours)
verdicts.reason: Pool A 69 x $0.2138 = $14.75, at $0.3413 = $23.55; pool B per-version October medians sum to $2.96 x 1.12 = $3.32 (PREREG $3.31, rounding), maxima $4.87 x 1.12 = $5.45; leak check about $0.001; margins 27/71/62/23/20 min recomputed from runs.csv wall times; 22.4 run-hours, about 3.0/3.0/1.6 h per round with 3 lanes. The $0.341 'high' per-run fee is a thinking-on run, so the high scenario is conservative. Recorded fees are the code's price-table estimate (same table at all versions), not the bill.

overall: The pre-registration is sound in its counts, version mapping, invocation and budget, and it already defines the thesis-hurting outcome. The review found and fixed 5 runner defects (an outcome-dependent re-run class, unrecoverable interrupted runs, re-run ordering across rounds, a leakage shift-test filter that would have disabled the test when the hosted model changed, and missing log fields) and about 17 under-specified points in sections A, B, D-G (zero variances, label precedence and reversed signs, R2 labels, tests missing for four 'confirmatory' rows, E3/E4 edge cases, a lenient and a non-falsifiable O2 reading, O2 lookup ambiguities, literature strata). Pool B is same-configuration in code (checked by content against the other commits with the same author date and subject: comment lines only), flags, question and mode. 5 of its 12 cells differ in launcher (October: 8 threads of one process sharing the fetch limiter); this is documented, with a sensitivity. All edits are marked 'v_prereg' and listed in PREREG.md 'Review changes (v_prereg)'. runs.json is unchanged. New SHA-256 list appended to FROZEN_HASHES.txt. Dry runs re-run (identical apart from clock lines). Decisions left to the user: how to freeze (commit and tag in the public repository, or hashes only); creating the 7 worktrees and junctions; 3 lanes vs one at a time; the second literature coder; the $30 stop's about $1 headroom over the conservative high scenario.
methodological_problems: K1/P2 compares a version-mixture gain with a gain on v2.17a, which is near the ceiling; the design has no same-configuration aggregation measurement on old code that is not conditioned on a catastrophic original, so P2 alone cannot separate an estimand change from a ceiling (caveat stated in PREREG A, not resolved).
o2_score.py prints only the direction of the gate reading; the pre-registered strength rule (Fisher exact vs in-sample 0/82) has to be computed in the O2 report from its counts.

The runner's live paths (thread scheduling, copying, --rerun-infra, the real leak check, --preflight) are tested only through helpers and dry runs; an exception in worker before its try block would leave a question marked as running and the loop waiting.
The request-identity check covers only the plan prompt and question text; judge, extraction and other prompts of old versions cannot be checked without running them.
Pool-A runs in the main checkout overwrite data/raw/agent/<qid>/<k>.txt of the same snapshot with v2.17a decoder text (local, gitignored; .raw bytes identical; no analysis script reads these files).
run.main writes a one-row results/agent/summary_<tag>.json per run, and pool-A tags are shared by 23 questions; harmless (scores are recomputed) but misleading.

Inherent and stated: a late-2026 repeat floor, not the archive's; the two test4 questions are backtest repeats of live-mode originals; the direct-ask check probes model memory through one prompt only; the 3 lanes depart from TOPIC_DECISION O3 'one at a time' (user decision).
